story.conflict: A bride must refuse to hide the groom's deception while he tries to make both women responsible for protecting him.
story.hook: The groom asked his bride to leave her own wedding. His wife had just arrived, and he wanted to explain things to her alone.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF NEITHER SHOULD HAVE STAYED
story.premise: A groom asks his bride to leave her own wedding when the wife he claimed to have divorced arrives.
story.punchline: He finally had the wedding to himself.
story.script: Claire asked which wife he meant. Ben had told her his divorce was finished six months ago. The woman at the door, Julia, said they'd had breakfast together that morning. He'd told her he was going to his cousin's wedding. Ben reached for Claire's elbow and told her to go home. He said Julia was upset and Claire was making it worse by standing there in her dress. Claire moved his hand. She wasn't going to disappear while he invented another explanation. Julia asked whether Claire knew they were married. Claire said she'd known about a marriage he claimed had ended. Ben told Julia they could sort this out privately if she stopped embarrassing him. She looked at the flowers, then at the guests. He'd brought her into a room full of people who believed she was his past. Claire asked him to tell everyone what he'd told her. He asked for five minutes. Julia said he'd had six months. Ben tried to follow Claire when she went to fetch her bag. Julia didn't block him or plead with him. She picked up her car keys. Outside, Claire's brother came over with the car. Julia asked whether she needed anything. Claire said she needed to go home. Ben was still waiting beside the flowers when both women left. He finally had the wedding to himself.
story.twist: The wife was told her husband was attending a cousin's wedding, while the bride was told the divorce was already complete.

youtube.description: A bride is told to leave her own wedding when the groom's wife arrives, exposing two very different stories about his marriage.
youtube.title: The Wife at the Wedding Door

story.conflict: A son must address the harm caused by his mother's public search without surrendering the independent life she wants him to leave.
story.hook: A man found his face on missing-person posters. His mother knew where he lived and wanted strangers to bring him home.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF MOVING OUT ISNT DISAPPEARING
story.premise: A mother puts her adult son on missing-person posters even though she knows where he lives and still speaks with him.
story.script: A stranger stopped Alex outside the supermarket and asked whether he was safe. Then she showed him the poster. His mother had used his graduation photograph and put her number underneath. Alex was thirty-two. He'd moved into his own flat three weeks ago and called her every Sunday. She had his address. He rang her there beside the shopping carts. She said she hadn't told anybody he was dead. Alex asked why that was supposed to make this better. She said he wasn't coming home when she asked, and perhaps somebody else could talk sense into him. Then his manager called. His mother had brought posters to reception. Alex told him he wasn't missing, and asked reception not to give out his address. His mother started crying. The house was quiet without him, and she'd kept his room ready. Alex said being lonely didn't make him lost. She asked whether she should throw his things away, then. He offered to collect the boxes on Saturday. That wasn't the answer she'd wanted. He also asked her to tell reception the truth and take down the posters she'd put up. She said people would think she'd been foolish. Alex said a stranger had just thought he needed rescuing from his own life. On Sunday, he called at the usual time. He told her what he'd cooked for dinner. From his own kitchen.
story.twist: The supposed disappearance is a voluntary move, and his mother is using strangers' concern to pressure him into returning.

youtube.description: An adult son discovers his mother's public search is an attempt to bring him back to the home he chose to leave.
youtube.title: The Missing Son in His Own Kitchen

story.conflict: A delivery worker must choose between protecting her pay and attending the funeral her employer treats as a ten-minute work stop.
story.hook: Her boss denied her time off for her father's funeral. Then he asked her to deliver his sympathy flowers to the service.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE BELONGED BESIDE HER MOTHER
story.premise: A boss refuses an employee leave for her father's funeral, then orders her to deliver his sympathy flowers to the service.
story.punchline: She took off her work jacket and sat beside her mother.
story.script: Nora checked the address twice. It was the chapel she'd booked with her mother. Her boss, Colin, placed a wreath in the van and told her to keep her work jacket on so people would know who'd sent it. The card said With Deepest Sympathy. Nora asked whether this meant she could stay. He said she had ten minutes, like any other delivery. They were short of drivers. She pointed out that he'd refused her unpaid leave a week ago. He said arguing would make her late. At the chapel, her brother came down the steps to help with the flowers. He asked why she was still in uniform. Nora said she was supposed to leave again. He looked at the card and asked who thought that was reasonable. Her phone rang before she answered. Colin wanted to know whether she'd finished. She said she'd delivered the wreath and was staying for her father's funeral. He said the rest of the shift would come out of her pay. Nora said she understood. Then he told her to show some respect for the people depending on her. Through the chapel doors, she could see her mother sitting alone in the front row. Nora said someone was depending on her here, too. She locked the van, switched off her phone, and went inside. She took off her work jacket and sat beside her mother.
story.twist: The employer wants his public gesture of sympathy delivered by the daughter whose own grief he refuses to accommodate.

youtube.description: A boss sends sympathy flowers to a funeral while refusing the grieving daughter time to attend it.
youtube.title: With Deepest Sympathy, Ten Minutes Only

story.conflict: A buyer must claim the home she paid for while the sellers use their son's supposed distress to justify keeping it.
story.hook: The sellers demanded rent from the woman who'd bought their house. She could sleep in the garage while they kept the bedrooms.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE HAD ALREADY PAID
story.premise: A couple who have sold their house demand rent from the buyer and offer her the garage while refusing to vacate the bedrooms.
story.punchline: Helen's bed was in her own bedroom.
story.script: Helen stood beside her moving van with the keys they'd handed over that morning. Paul said his son couldn't cope with leaving. His wife added that Helen had no children, so she wouldn't understand. Helen asked why accepting her payment hadn't been the moment to mention this. Paul said the garage was spacious, and two hundred a week would help with their expenses. She asked whether they expected her to pay for a house and then pay them to use it. His wife said she was making a difficult day worse. Their son, Josh, came downstairs carrying a box. He asked why Helen's movers were waiting outside. Paul told him they were sorting out somewhere for Helen to stay. Josh said the house was hers. His mother said he wasn't ready to leave. He put his box down and asked when she'd asked him. He'd already packed. The hotel she'd said was booked wasn't booked at all. Paul admitted they'd hoped Helen would give them another month. Helen said she hadn't agreed to become their lodger. Josh carried his box to their car. His mother stopped beside the height marks on the kitchen doorframe and started crying. Helen offered to take a photograph for her. She didn't offer a bedroom. By evening, the marks were in a photograph, their boxes were in the car, and Helen's bed was in her own bedroom.
story.twist: The son is ready to move and discovers his parents have been speaking for him to avoid facing their own departure.

youtube.description: A house buyer arrives to find the sellers demanding rent, with their son offered as the reason they cannot leave.
youtube.title: Two Hundred a Week for Her Own Garage
